# requires: logging
#
# The same call, six machines, six answers. Nothing in this scenario names a
# path, a host or a service, which is the rule being tested: the code that logs
# does not choose the rung, and the same program on two machines lands in two
# different places without changing a line.
#
# `auto` and `write` are deliberately different questions. `auto` reports the
# rung the machine's configuration selects; `write` reports where one record
# actually landed. A configured service that nothing is listening on is still
# the rung, and every record it takes goes below it -- which is why a degraded
# service must not be reported as a degraded configuration.
machine none
auto A
separation A
write A
default
machine file
auto B
write B
default
machine service+file
auto C
write C
machine deaf+file
auto D
write D
machine unwritable
auto E
write E
machine deaf
auto F
write F

# expect 2: ok tier=discard [LOG-S3]
# expect 3: ok sep=none [LOG-P1]
# expect 4: ok where=discard [LOG-S3]
# expect 5: ok out=stderr [LOG-S8]
# expect 7: ok tier=file [LOG-S1] [LOG-S2]
# expect 8: ok where=file [LOG-S2]
# expect 9: ok out=sink [LOG-S8]
# expect 11: ok tier=service [LOG-S1] [LOG-S2]
# expect 12: ok where=service [LOG-S2]
# expect 14: ok tier=service [LOG-S2]
# expect 15: ok where=file [LOG-S5]
# expect 17: ok tier=discard [LOG-S4]
# expect 18: ok where=discard [LOG-S4]
# expect 20: ok tier=service [LOG-S2]
# expect 21: ok where=discard [LOG-S5]
